images.caption: Figure 1:DexEngineturns human demonstrations into physically executable data for a whole bimanual robot, in under 5 GPU-minutes per clip.

Figure 2:DexEngine pipeline.Human demonstrations are split into clips, a scene placement that the arms reach without penetration is found, and the resulting kinematic reference is corrected in physics simulation. The corrected motions become train-ready data for four robot hands, with pose and visual augmentation. Red marks penetration in the kinematic reference, and green the corrected contact.

Figure 3:Reachability map. (a) Map cells, 96 orientations each. (b) IK solutions stored for the purple pose. (c) Screening: a frame is covered (green) if a stored pose (purple) lies in the3×3×33\times 3\times 3cells around its target, and uncovered (red) otherwise.

Figure 4:IK and retiming. (a) Elbow swivel: per-frame IK (gray), coarse path (navy), runs from it (green, passes) and from random configurations (red; highlighted: wrist>>3 cm off). (b) Joint speed over limit; spans above1/1.151/1.15(dashed;Sec.B.8) stretch (yellow).

Figure 5:From human sequences to robot data. (a) Clips passing data preparation (1), reference generation (2) and physics correction (3), by dataset, averaged over the four hands. (b) Failures that remove clips at each step (red).

Table 2:Pipelines on the same 64 TACO clips with the SharpA hand, whereKKclips share one policy. Left: ADD-AUC, SP-SR and MP-SR against GPU-minutes per clip (log scale), each method marked by the symbol before its name. Orange marks the floating hand and blue the arm-mounted hand. Circles are ours, and light fill marks our dataset’s setting. Bold: best. Method changes:Sec.E.2.

Figure 6:Data and policies. Row 1: one Wuji 2 training data frame per task in kinematic data and in ours, close to the hand, from the scene named above; arrows mark the finger link the kinematic reference pushes deepest into the object (yellow; red: its part inside the object; inset: the same frame, object see-through). Row 2: GR00T N1.7 trained on kinematic replay and on ours, in simulation at the same time step of that scene, and the policy trained on ours on the real robot. Row 3: our data, one clip per source dataset, hand named above.

Figure S1:Per hand, recorded trajectories whose deepest penetration of an arm or its hand into the torso or the other arm exceedsxx. Legend: the excluded share, beyond 2 cm (Tab.S12). Max: deepest (mm) of a curve leaving the axis.

Figure S2:Visual augmentation of the real-robot fine-tuning data (Wuji 2 hands).
Rows: the P&P, Pour and Sweep clips ofTab.5, one placement variant each.
Left: the exo camera under the fixed appearance.
Right: the left-eye ego camera at the same frame under five of its 35 appearances, which randomize the materials, lighting and distractor objects and change the colors of the manipulated objects, including the green of our 3D prints.

Figure S3:One recorded episode (HO-Cap clip, Wuji 2 hands) with all its streams, in the rows ofTab.S3.
The numbered exo frames mark their times on the plots.
Dots on the left-eye frames and the bottom strip give the force of the hands on the box, which passes from the left hand to the right.
Sim-only marks the privileged streams ofTab.S3, which only the simulator provides.

Figure S4:Pose and visual augmentation of one two-handed TACO clip (Wuji 2 hands): the right hand scrapes a knife across the bowl that the left hand holds.
Rows: the original placement and three pose-augmentation variants, each simulated again.
Columns: the fixed and the four random appearances of visual augmentation, which change only the images.

Figure S5:Recorded episodes from the nine source datasets on the four robot hands, half of them under a random appearance of visual augmentation.
Ego view, but exo view for the one-hand clips of HRDexDB and DexCanvas, where the arm hides the hand from the head camera.

Figure S6:The four robot hands.
(a) Three two-handed clips, each on the four hands at the same moment of the human demonstration.
(b) Episodes from six source datasets per hand, none of them shown elsewhere in this section.
Dots: force of each hand link on the manipulated objects, on the scale ofFig.S3.
